questions.q: A caller says he is from your bank and asks for the OTP you just received. You should —
options: Refuse — banks never ask for OTPs
Share it if he knows your name
questions.solution: **No genuine bank ever asks for OTP/PIN/CVV** — an OTP shared is money gone.

questions.q: Which statement about **analog computers** is correct?
options: They work on discrete binary digits
They are faster than all digital supercomputers
They were invented in the fourth generation
questions.solution: Analog computers **measure** continuous quantities — temperature, pressure, voltage, speed — and work directly on those signals. They predate digital machines and are not used for general computing today.
questions.shortcut: Analog = 'a needle that slides', not digits.

questions.q: A running slideshow is closed with —
questions.solution: **Esc exits the show** and returns to Normal editing view.

questions.q: During **execution** of an instruction, the actual work (say adding two numbers) is done by the —
questions.solution: After fetch and decode, the **execute** step hands real computation to the **ALU**; the CU only supervises, and the PC merely points to the next instruction.
questions.shortcut: Decode is CU's job; the sums are ALU's job.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "I shall start the classes next Monday."
options: He said that he would start the classes next Monday.
He said that he will start the classes the following Monday.
He said that he would start the classes the following Monday.
He said that he would start the classes that Monday.
questions.solution: shall steps to **would** and next Monday becomes **the following Monday**. 'Next Monday' stays anchored to the vanished speaking day; 'will start' shifts the time word but not the modal; 'that Monday' is the wrong time family — that pairs with today, not with next.
questions.shortcut: next → the following; shall → would. Both move.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.solution: The regulars compare two kinds of quiet — library quiet and home quiet where 'the television mutters'. The sentence says the library quiet has a different ___ : the word for the *character* of a thing is **quality**. Quiet has no price, length or colour here; the next clause describes its nature, not its cost or duration.
questions.shortcut: Ask what the following clause describes (the character of the quiet) and name it.
questions.passage: The corporation library on Gandhi Road now stays open till eleven at night. The change began when a clerk noticed students reading under the streetlight after closing time. The reading hall, once half (1) ______, is now full by eight o'clock. Regulars say the quiet here has a different (2) ______ from the quiet of their homes, where the television mutters in every room. The librarian has also begun to (3) ______ old newspapers for a small archive that students use to trace how an issue developed. Pleased by the response, the corporation has sanctioned two more fans, and the students (4) ______ full advantage of the extended hours.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Entrepreneur** = entre + pre + neur, from French. The ending is **-eur** (like connoisseur), and there is an r after the second p.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: **Teach someone** is followed by the to-infinitive: taught him **to be** patient. 'Taught him being patient' is wrong; a bare *be* cannot follow the object here; *been* needs 'has/had'.
questions.shortcut: teach + object + to-infinitive — no meaning test needed, only the pattern.
questions.passage: Every morning before his duty, Ravi, a city bus driver, spends an hour in his small garden behind the staff quarter. He grows tomatoes in paint buckets because the soil in his yard (1) ______ too rocky for beds. His neighbours at first (2) ______ fun of the buckets, but now three of them copy the idea. Ravi says gardening has taught him (3) ______ patient, and patience is what city traffic demands. When a passenger once praised the chillies he carried in his bag, Ravi (4) ______ him a bucket of his own the very next day.

questions.q: The **Abel Prize**, since 2003 called the 'Nobel of mathematics', is awarded by which country?
questions.solution: **Norway** (by its Academy of Science and Letters) gives the Abel Prize; the Fields Medal is the other great mathematics award.

questions.q: The Duncan Passage lies between:
questions.solution: **Duncan Passage** separates **South Andaman** from **Little Andaman**. Coco Channel = North Andaman | Coco Islands; Ten Degree Channel = Little Andaman | Car Nicobar; Great Channel = Great Nicobar | Sumatra.

questions.q: **The Republic**, the foundational text of Western political philosophy, was written by:
questions.solution: **Plato's** The Republic discusses justice and the ideal state; Aristotle wrote Politics.

questions.q: The city once called **Constantinople** is today known as:
questions.solution: **Constantinople** was renamed **Istanbul** (officially from 1930); Ankara is Turkey's capital. Peking-Beijing and Rangoon-Yangon are parallel cases.

questions.q:
A pie chart shows a family's monthly budget of ₹72,000. The central angles are:

| Head | Food | Rent | Education | Transport | Savings | Others |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Angle | 108° | 72° | 54° | 36° | 45° | 45° |

How much more is spent on Food than on Education?
Two similar triangles have perimeters $24$ cm and $36$ cm. If the area of the larger triangle is $54$ sq cm, the area of the smaller triangle is:
questions.solution:
Side ratio $= \frac{24}{36} = \frac{2}{3}$, so the area ratio is $\frac{4}{9}$.

Smaller area $= 54 \times \frac{4}{9} = 24$ sq cm.

questions.q: A sum of ₹2,550 is divided among A, B and C such that A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 2 : 5. C's share is:
What is the unit digit of $7^{95} \times 3^{58}$?

In the following series, one number is **wrong**. Find the wrong number.

**1, 8, 27, 64, 124, 216**
How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: Lines through the apex = 5 inner lines + 2 sides = 7. Any two of them make one triangle on a base: C(7, 2) = (6 × 7)/2 = 21. Total = **21**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**124, 217, 342, 999**
questions.shortcut: Add 1 to each number and look for a cube.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **CFIL : DHLP :: GJMP : ?**
questions.solution: The shifts rise: C+1 = D, F+2 = H, I+3 = L, L+4 = P — tuple (+1, +2, +3, +4). Apply it to GJMP: G+1 = H, J+2 = L, M+3 = P, P+4 = T → **HLPT**.
questions.shortcut: Copy the whole tuple exactly; do not average or 'tidy' it.
